7TH ST. AUTO — PICK YOUR WHIP

Flashy whips pull clout — and eyes. Low-key cars keep you invisible. Your whip waits on the street out front: walk up and press A to drive. Behind the wheel, B steps out. Cars stay on the streets — stop at a CITY LIMIT corner to change hoods. Own a whip and the shop will build it up: Stock → Tuned → Street → Pro → Kingpin, each tier a notch faster.

UPGRADES

Enforcers post up at your trap houses — home hood first — and step in when trouble comes to the house. They don't follow you; the open street is yours alone. They eat $40 a day each while you're a Rookie — and the wage climbs $25 a rank as your name grows. Miss payroll and they walk. Hustlers and up can also run CREW MOVES from here: rob a rival, or tip a raid on one.

      HOW TO PLAY

      Move: drag the stick (bottom-left) in any direction — push further to go faster — or WASD / arrow keys. Hold B (or Shift) to run. Guide: the little arrow badge rides the edge of the screen and always points at your next move, with the distance. When the goal changes it spells the move out for a few seconds, then shrinks back to just the arrow — follow it. Interact: press A (or E) when the A bubble pops over a person or a door — A talks, interacts, confirms, nothing else. B is your other hand: hold it to run, tap it to back out of a menu, pass on a lick, or step out of your car. When a spot has more than one thing to do (the Corner Store, say), A opens a little choice list — flick the stick ↑↓ + A to pick, B to back out, or just tap one. The loop: work the store, or trade — buy product cheap at The Spot in one district, ride the transit stop (top of the block), sell high in another. Spend cash to raise clout. Carrying product warms up your heat and full pockets attract jackboys; pay off the cop, rest at the hotel, or lay low at home. Getting away resets it: break far away from Reed (or a jackboy) and hold that distance, and your wanted level drops straight to zero — while heat's 55+ the meter shows ★ WANTED and Reed is actively hunting you. The city: thirteen hoods, called by their street names — DTW (Over-the-Rhine), Campus (Clifton), West Side (Westwood), MTA (Mt Auburn), Uptown (College Hill), Over the Water (Covington), plus Avondale, Price Hill, Walnut Hills, the West End, Bond Hill, Evanston and Madisonville. Every Spot pays different prices that shift daily — watch for CHEAP and HOT PRICE tags, and rumors in the travel menu. Over the Water: Covington, Kentucky side, pays the most for Starlight in the city — but Reed watches the bridges. With heat at 30+ you cross carrying 10 units or less. The story: it never ends. A chapter is always up — deliver product across town, stack fresh earnings, or serve licks before the deadline for cash + clout. Close one and the next writes itself, a little harder. Your current chapter sits at the top of the objectives and the guide chip points at it. Licks vs wholesale: The Spot buys bulk, fast, at street price. Licks (the $ badges wandering each district) pay more per piece, one small deal at a time — but every deal is a small heat event, and some are setups. A lick shops your pockets: he asks for what you're actually carrying, and pays a premium for the right good in the right hood at the right hour — Fizz flies on the morning rush, Starlight peaks at club hours. The market and travel screens call out what's hot right now. Under 10 clout you can't cold-approach a lick yourself — he'll size you up and wave you off — but his step is always his choice: the block sends somebody to flag you down every so often at ANY rep, so the street never sits dead. Walk-ups scale per hood: while you're unknown they're slower and warier; as your rep grows — and faster if you deal fair (at or under street), which builds LOVE — they flag you down constantly, on foot and at the car window (A serves, B passes). Squeeze prices over street (taxing) or rob their people and that hood holds a GRUDGE: half the walk-ups, half the rep earned, until fair deals and time cool it. Either way you can always grind it back — nobody's ever fully shut out. Robbing a lick: every lick battle has a ROB HIM choice. Take his cash — or his whole pack, if he's holding — but it always costs clout (word gets around, and the loss floats over your head with the reason), your rep in that hood takes the same hit, and heat spikes hard win or lose. He might fight back and take your money, or bolt screaming and bring the whole block's eyes. Piece-buyers are soft targets; pack-holders carry more; a bulk buyer is carrying the most money and is the likeliest to scrap. A strap and a crew even the odds. Robbed licks dip and won't deal for a while — and the whole hood holds a GRUDGE (see Licks vs wholesale): half the walk-ups and half the rep until you make it right. Cars: 7th St. Auto sells a low-key beater and a flashy coupe. Flashy pulls clout fast and draws jackboys; low-key keeps heat and attention down. Your whip waits on the street in front of the lot — walk up and press A to get in. Cars live on the streets: no sidewalks, no cutting through the block, and folks hop out of your way. Behind the wheel you flow with traffic — quick, not teleporty — and the lot can build your whip up five tiers (Stock → Kingpin) for more top end. B steps out and parks it. Stop at the end of any street — the CITY LIMIT corners — and the hoods list opens: pick your hood and roll in, no fare (the bridge rule still applies heading Over the Water). Crossing into a new hood is a clean getaway: heat drops to zero and no cop or jackboy follows you over the line. Licks serve the car too: one will walk up to your window with the same offer — A serves, B passes. BATTLES — Pokémon style: Everything serious is a battle screen now. Licks haggle — they lowball you, you ACCEPT / COUNTER / PUSH / WALK and they counter back. Reed stops you — FIGHT / RUN / BRIBE (pick your price: $50 clears 1 star + 2 min grace, $150 clears 2 + 5 min, $400 clears ALL stars + 10 min where cops ignore you — the countdown rides by your stars) / COMPLY. Jackboys — FIGHT (way better STRAPPED) / BRIBE $60 / RUN / GIVE IT UP. Tap a choice or press 1–6 for the numbered pick. Battles don't take B-cancel — you picked this life. STRAP: Buy a gun for $180 at The Spot market (bottom row). It lives on you — +~30% to win fights vs jackboys, Reed, trap guards and turf crews. Every battle screen lists it next to your name. ROB THE TRAP: At any Spot door, A opens ENTER MARKET or ROB THE TRAP — shoot it out with the guard for cash + product (big heat, big clout), GRAB & RUN for a safer snatch, or bribe the guard $50. TRAP HOUSES: every hood has a trap house of its own — a separate boarded-up building (not The Spot) with a FOR SALE sign and its price on it: $2,500 in the cheap hoods, $5,000–$8,000 mid-city, $12,000–$15,000 in DTW and Over the Water. Buy it and the sign flips, the windows light up in your colors, licks start loitering out front getting served, and your enforcers post up there as guards. The house works on its own — no stocking runs and no deliveries. It cooks Fizz, Moon Candy and the odd Glitter, and every cook pays out on its own — cash and product land straight on you, no collecting, ever. Spend cash to upgrade through four tiers for faster product, more money per day, and bigger storage. And the house is a safe house: duck in its door (A) and any cop chase or jackboy hunt breaks on the spot — heat cools while you're inside and nobody can grab you in there. Its tier and rates show at the door and in YOUR TRAPS below. BUSINESSES: every hood also has a store (striped awning) and a bar (neon sign) with FOR SALE boards on them — stores run $2,000–$6,000, bars $4,000–$10,000 depending on the hood. Buy one at its door and it pays you on its own, straight to your pocket with a "+$ from …" toast — no collecting. Stores pay a steady rate day and night; bars pay more and jump to a night rate after dark. Buying a bar also puts your name on the door: a one-time +3 rep in that hood. All twenty-six, their rates and your total passive income per minute live in the BUSINESSES panel in this menu. TURF WARS & HOOD REP: Clout is now per-hood (REP rides next to the hood name in the top bar; your home hood starts known at 30, everywhere else starts at 6). Serving licks, wholesale and winning fights builds rep in that hood. Hustle in a foreign hood under 20 rep and the local crew may step up — FIGHT FOR TURF, PAY TAX $75, NAME-DROP TRVP, or RUN. Win/pay and the deal you were making still goes through. Crew & tiers: the CREW button up top starts your gang and hires enforcers — they post up at your trap houses (home hood first) and only step in when trouble comes to the house. At Hustler the same menu unlocks CREW MOVES: send jackboys to rob a rival ($500), or tip the law to raid one ($300) — one of each per day. Earn clout + achievements to climb Rookie → Hustler → Boss → Kingpin — bigger pockets, better wholesale rates, bigger licks. Kingpin is gated now: it takes 10 achievements AND 7 days since your account was created — no more one-day kingpins. Clout only cools while you're standing still laying low — every point that moves floats over your head and lands in the street log with the reason. Carry more, carry bigger: your carry is a ladder. At The Spot you can cop Deep Pockets (38 units), then the Duffel Backpack (65 units — Hustlers and up), then the Big Duffle (110 units — Bosses and up), and it keeps climbing: Cargo Duffel (180), Stash Trunk (260), Stash Hauler (380) and the Empire Rig (550 — Kingpins only). Your tier adds +5 units a rank on top. The BAG chip in the top bar shows what you're wearing. Your pockets hold all the cash you can grab — no limit — but every dollar riding on you can be taken by a jackboy or seized in a bust. The Stash is the only safe money: stash the bag after a big flip and nothing touches it. Bigger loads mean fewer wasted trips. THE STASH — your bank: tap STASH up top (or press V) anytime. Money stashed in the Trvp Stash cannot be taken by jackboys, Reed, or a bust — only pocket cash is at risk on the street. The Stash pays 1% every in-game day. Stash the bag after a big flip, keep a little walking money, and a robbery stops hurting so bad. Different faces, different hoods: every hood answers to its own kingpin — Big Lou runs DTW, Brickman runs MTA, E da God runs the West Side, and Ace, Chris, Cap and the rest hold their own corners. The kingpin posts your package runs and the mission board (his own run pays the most), and his crew is who steps to you when your rep's low. Names, fits, faces and who'll even talk to you change when you cross town. The menu panel below lists who's who in the hood you're standing in. Every hood builds its own block: cross town and the buildings themselves move — different corners, colors and signs, the club, store, hotel and lot all dressed in local colors, and the court repainted with the hood's mark. Each hood also has one landmark that's its own: Findlay Market in DTW, the Zoo gates in Avondale, the Esquire in Campus, the Incline in Price Hill, Union Terminal in the West End, Mainstrasse Over the Water, Cincinnati Gardens in Bond Hill, the Cintas Center in Evanston, the Depot in Madisonville. The six joints you use are always there — you just have to learn each hood's streets. THE MISSION BOARD: The Spot is a mission board now, not just a market. Its board posts runs to other hoods: DELIVERIES (pick up a package here, drop it at their Spot), COLLECTIONS (grab a stash there, haul it home), and HITS (rob their trap or a rival's stash — paid the second it's done). Pay scales with the length of the road and how mean the hood is. One run at a time, on a real clock, and the arrow walks you through every leg — heat, jackboys and turf crews all live out on that road. They still run up on you: Officer Reed, jackboys and turf crews still chase and step to you in the open — that pressure is the game. What changed is pacing: every NPC now runs on cooldown timers (see below), so the block can't machine-gun you with encounters. PACKS — free product in the wild: every 40–60 seconds a stash pack glows up somewhere on the block (watch for the pulsing bag). Walk over it to grab it: free product for your pockets — sometimes a little cash folded in. Packs lean toward whatever the hood moves. Don't sleep: one pack at a time, and the next won't drop while you're still holding the last one's glow. Cooldown timers — the street breathes: nobody can be spammed anymore. After a lick deal, that lick cools down ~24s before he'll buy again and ~14s before he walks up again; Reed needs ~12s to reset after a stop; a jackboy hunt leaves a ~35s quiet window; turf crews give a hood ~45s of peace after stepping to you; even talking has a short cooldown. Cooldowns tick on every NPC — if someone's cooling down, the prompt tells you how long. It keeps the game from running too fast and makes every run-up actually mean something. Work has weight: jobs don't chain anymore. A finished board run leaves the kingpin ~2 minutes to line up fresh runs, scrapping one costs the board a minute, the kingpin needs ~75s before his next package, and the corner-store register takes a real 90-second break between shifts. Every one of those timers shows live on the STREET PACE panel below — plan the wait: flip product, serve licks, let your traps pay out, and the next run lands right on time. Trvp's ship menu: talk to him and the saucer comes down — power-up drops, guidance that reads your situation, claimable challenges, your empire math, and space weapons. The leaderboard lives up in this menu instead — real accounts on this device only. Trvp: your alien guide. Talk to him by the apartments — the ship lands for it — or press T to call a power-up drop. Press G to spend the power you're holding. SPACE WEAPONS: Trvp sells alien hardware on his ship menu — a Zorp Ray (1 charge, +95% fight odds) or a Nova Blaster (3 charges, +50%, Bosses only). Stronger than any store gun, but every fight burns a charge and then it's scrap. One at a time, cash up front, ship recharges between sales. The FIGHT button in any battle shows the weapon and charges left while you hold one.

      WHO'S WHO

      You — your username rides over your head, in the fit you picked when you made your account. The Kingpin — every hood has one (Big Lou in DTW, Brickman in MTA, E da God on the West Side). He runs the trap house corner and posts the paid runs. Do right by him. Officer Reed — patrols the block. Bribe him when heat is high. Jackboy — shows up when your clout gets loud. Don't let him touch you. Trvp — alien guide posted up by the apartments. Talk to him and the saucer lands: power-ups, guidance, challenges, space weapons. Or call the ship (T) for a drop. Licks — buyers wandering every district with a $ badge. Better money than wholesale, one risky little deal at a time. Your crew — enforcers you hire post up guarding your trap houses. Trouble that comes to the house meets them first.

      Prototype slice: thirteen Cincinnati neighborhoods — DTW, Avondale, Campus, Price Hill, Walnut Hills, West End, West Side, MTA, Uptown, Over the Water, Bond Hill, Evanston, Madisonville — trading, cars, crews, tiers and an endless story on one shared block each. Real multiplayer, dating, alliances and live community features need the native app + backend — the versions here are playable stubs and design previews.

        YOUR EMPIRE

        YOUR TRAPS — THEY WORK ON THEIR OWN

        Buy it, upgrade it — it pays you on its own. Every owned trap keeps cooking product and stacking cash until its storage fills, and every cook deposits cash + product straight to you. No deliveries, no collecting, ever. The house itself is a safe house: duck in the door to shake heat.

        BUSINESSES — STORES & BARS

        Every hood has a store and a bar with a FOR SALE sign on them. Buy one and it pays you on its own — revenue lands straight in your pocket with a "+$ from …" toast, no collecting. Stores pay steady; bars pay more, jump after dark, and put a one-time +3 rep on your name in that hood.

        YOUR STASH

        Tap STASH up top to move money. Stash cash survives jackboys and busts; pocket cash doesn't.
